historical_reviews.v3_1: A valid fault injection must prove one mapped fan's transition as a synchronized chain: commanded physical obstruction, RPM/status fault threshold, amber LED assertion and matching SEL identity, followed by obstruction removal, RPM stabilization, LED extinction and a matching recovery event. A generic fan alarm or later-normal snapshot is insufficient.

original_test_intent: Validate one identified fan's physical-failure detection and recovery through BMC sensor/SEL state and the local amber fault LED without damaging the cooling system.
original_method: Record the exact fan and complete healthy baseline, have an authorized operator apply the approved flexible non-conductive obstruction for a strictly bounded interval while an observer captures the LED and the Agent timestamps full fan/thermal/power/SEL state, remove the obstruction immediately after the required assertion, then prove stable RPM, LED-off and correlated SEL recovery without clearing logs.
manual_activity: A cooling/platform owner approves the exact fan, safe obstruction fixture, maximum duration and abort limits; an authorized operator applies and removes the obstruction, an observer verifies the LED, and the owner decides the verdict.
required_inputs: Expected SEL assertion and deassertion signatures
Workload drain or safe load envelope
Emergency removal and platform recovery procedure
safety_requirements: Never stop a fan with any body part or conductive/rigid object
Require explicit owner authorization and an on-site operator
Use only the approved fan and obstruction fixture
Bound the obstruction by time and thermal limits
Remove the obstruction immediately on vibration, damage, abnormal sound or thermal excursion
Do not repeat a failed or ambiguous jam
Continuously observe all cooling and power health
agent_execution_scope: Verify target identity and approved test envelope
Timestamp full fan/RPM/temperature/power and SEL evidence during the operator action
Correlate sensor and SEL records to the selected fan
Collect recovery telemetry after the operator removes the obstruction
Archive evidence and report without verdict
engineer_actions: Approve fan mapping, fixture, duration and abort limits
Authorize and supervise the physical action
Stop the test on any unsafe condition
Resolve missing or mismatched fault identity
Approve recovery or invoke platform recovery

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: DeepSeek supplies no executable command because the decisive stimulus and LED check are physical. That boundary is correct, but read-only BMC sensor/SEL collection remains useful only as supporting evidence synchronized to the operator action.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the platform-approved read-only IPMI/Redfish interfaces to capture unfiltered fan, thermal, power and SEL state before, during and after the single authorized obstruction; do not use any command that changes fan policy or clears logs.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The one-fan fault/recovery sequence and 6-minute source estimate remain, but the physical duration is governed by the shorter owner-approved thermal limit.

modernized_recommendation.status: OPERATOR-DRIVEN SINGLE-FAN FAULT WITH SYNCHRONIZED BMC AND LED EVIDENCE
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a fan identity map and synchronized timeline so the physical fan, RPM/status transition, amber LED and SEL assertion/recovery are demonstrated as one bounded event, followed by stable cooling recovery.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds explicit fan correlation, independent observation, strict stall/thermal limits, continuous whole-platform cooling monitoring and a no-repeat rule while preserving the intended physical stimulus.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A photograph alone cannot prove the BMC selected the correct fan, and an SEL entry alone cannot prove the local LED or safe mechanical recovery; both evidence paths are required.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A powered stalled fan can heat its motor, stress blades or bearings and reduce platform cooling; the Agent cannot judge physical contact safety or visually verify the LED.

project_override_considerations: Approve a vendor-safe obstruction fixture instead of ad hoc contact, the exact fan/LED/sensor map, RPM and debounce thresholds, maximum stall interval, thermal/power aborts, permitted workload and the recovery deadline for this chassis.
expected_evidence: Approved procedure, fan identity/map, obstruction fixture, duration and abort limits
SUT/BMC/firmware identity, workload state, operator/observer and synchronized timestamps
Complete baseline, fault and recovery fan/RPM/temperature/power telemetry
Fan-specific SEL assertion and recovery records
Amber-on and off visual evidence tied to the same fan and timeline
Stable post-recovery health, preserved logs, no-repeat audit and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently target a physical fan jam, BMC fault/recovery evidence and amber LED behavior. The generic request to clear logs is unsafe execution guidance, not a conflict in the test identity or acceptance target.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The approved physical method, operator, fan map and limits are concrete prerequisites, so classification is REQUIRES. Execution remains unavailable until they are supplied, but the case definition itself is reviewable.

review_improvement: Converts a blanket manual-only conclusion into a controlled hybrid workflow that keeps mechanical and visual work human-owned while requiring fan-specific, synchronized BMC evidence and a proven safe recovery.
independent_technical_reasoning: A fan stall is not established merely because RPM falls: the system must identify the same physical fan, cross its defined fault threshold after debounce, assert the corresponding LED and SEL event, then reverse those states within approved recovery limits. Because a powered stalled motor and lost airflow can damage hardware before generic alarms appear, obstruction duration and whole-platform thermal state are first-class acceptance controls, not incidental precautions.
